sections.html:
Sandy Springs is an office-and-hospital suburb in northern Fulton County. Sellers deal with county offices for valuation and tax billing, and with city hall for permits. The city spans 38.52 square miles, and its population was 108,080 at the 2020 count with an estimate of 105,013 for 2025.

The city borders Atlanta to the south, Dunwoody and Brookhaven to the east, and the Chattahoochee River to the west and north. Hospitals and corporate offices make up much of the job base, so the buyer pool often includes people who work at the medical campuses or the Perimeter Center towers. Georgia 400, I-285, Roswell Road (U.S. 19) and Georgia 9 carry most traffic, and three MARTA rail stops serve the city: Medical Center, Sandy Springs and North Springs. Houses near the stations and the 400 and 285 interchange tend to be described by their commute, so give buyers an honest drive or ride time.

One district can draw a very different buyer than another. The city's districts include:

  • City Springs: the downtown district north of I-285, with apartments replacing older strip malls along Roswell Road.
  • Riverside: the hilly western district along the Chattahoochee.
  • The Panhandle: a strip between the river and Dunwoody, reached from the Northridge Road exit of Georgia 400.
  • Perimeter Center: the commercial area around Perimeter Mall, including most office towers and the hospital cluster known as Pill Hill.
  • North Springs: the northern district served by the North Springs MARTA station.
  • South Springs: the part below I-285 that buyers call inside the Perimeter.

Know which district your house sits in and describe it plainly, whether the draw is the commute, the river or the school zone. Fulton County School System runs the public schools, and attendance zones differ by street, so buyers will check the exact address on the school system's lookup before making an offer.

sections.h2: Which repairs need a City of Sandy Springs permit?
sections.html:
Most structural work needs a residential building permit, issued by the permit desk at City Hall, 1 Galambos Way. Owners apply online, and a technician can meet you by appointment. The city's page sets out what triggers a permit and what does not:

  • A permit is required whenever an owner builds, alters, enlarges or repairs a building or accessory structure, and also for deck or patio replacements and generator installations.
  • Painting and carpeting generally need no permit.
  • Detached structures under 120 square feet need no building permit but may still face Development Code rules.
  • Flat roof replacement needs a permit; replacing individual shingles on a pitched roof does not.
  • Fire or storm repair within the original footprint falls under a reconstruction permit, and emergency stabilization may begin first if the permit is applied for within 48 hours or the next business day.

Contractors with a state license can pull permits, and so can an owner for the home where that owner currently lives. If you have been renting the house out, plan on hiring a contractor for anything beyond cosmetic work.

sections.h2: Fulton County assessments and tax bills
sections.html:
The county's Board of Assessors sets value, and the Fulton tax commissioner's office sends the bill that covers the county, the schools and the City of Sandy Springs. Notices go out each summer, owners get 45 days to appeal from the date of the notice, and filing works online, through the mail or at an assessors' office.

Homeowners who miss the April 1 homestead deadline can still apply during that 45-day appeal period. Because the bill attaches to the property for the whole year, anyone closing late in the year should decide in the contract who pays it and confirm with the closing attorney how it will appear on the settlement statement.

The North Fulton service center of the Board of Assessors is at 7741 Roswell Road NE, Suite 210, and the main phone line is 404-612-6440.

sections.h2: Who pays the Georgia transfer tax?
sections.html:
Title transfers in Georgia carry a state excise tax. The seller owes it, and many contracts move the cost to the buyer. The state sets the rate at a flat $1 on the first $1,000, then 10 cents for each further $100 or part of $100.

Payment comes first. Only then will the superior court clerk record the deed and stamp it as paid. The declaration, Form PT-61, goes in electronically through the clerks' cooperative authority, and exemption questions go to the Fulton County clerk. Check the transfer tax clause in your contract, since it decides who writes that check.

sections.h2: Can a former Sandy Springs short-term rental be sold?
sections.html:
Yes, and the first thing to settle is the city's lodging tax record. Sandy Springs requires hotels, motels and short-term rentals to collect occupancy tax from guests and remit it by the 20th of each month for the prior month, with a completed return. Returns paid on time earn a vendor credit of 3 percent of the tax collected. Late payments lose that credit and may carry penalties and interest.

If you operated a rental, file any missing returns and pay what you owe before you list, because a buyer's attorney may ask for proof. Mail goes to the Business Occupation and Excise Tax Division at 1 Galambos Way, and the Permits and Revenue Office at City Hall can help with filing. If the house sits in a subdivision, also read your association covenants, since they can restrict rentals separately from city rules.

sections.h2: Who handles which part of a sale?
sections.html:
Several offices touch a sale, and each answers a different question.

Where Sandy Springs sellers take each property question
QuestionOfficeDetail
Is my value fair?Fulton County Board of AssessorsAppeal window of 45 days after the notice
Who sends my tax bill?Fulton County Tax CommissionerCollects for the county, schools and Sandy Springs
Do I need a permit?City permitting office, 1 Galambos WayRequired for building, altering or repairing
Rental tax owed?Business Occupation and Excise Tax DivisionOccupancy tax due the 20th of each month
Who pays transfer tax?Georgia Department of RevenueSeller is liable unless the contract says otherwise

The realistic paths are a conventional listing, an as-is sale to an investor, or a direct cash sale when timing outranks top price. Compare net proceeds, not only the headline number. A direct cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval and appraisal, which is why it can close sooner when title is clear. A listing can still net more for a house in good order, so ask for the figure after taxes, liens and closing costs from each route and read them side by side.

faqs.q: How fast can a Sandy Springs house sell for cash?
faqs.a: A cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal and loan approval, so it can close sooner than a listing when title is clear. A listing adds showings, inspections and the buyer's financing.

faqs.q: Do I owe transfer tax on a Sandy Springs sale?
faqs.a: Legally the seller owes it, though a contract can hand the cost to the buyer. The state's rate is a flat $1 on the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each further $100.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Fulton value after listing?
faqs.a: Only during the 45 days after your notice was issued. When that window shuts, the year's value stands, so find the deadline on the notice itself.

faqs.q: What if I rented the house short term?
faqs.a: Pay any unpaid city lodging tax before closing. Monthly returns fall due on the 20th, and filing late gives up the 3 percent vendor credit.

faqs.q: Does a new roof need a permit before I sell?
faqs.a: A flat roof replacement needs one, but replacing individual shingles on a pitched roof does not. Call the city permitting office if your project falls in between.
